candidates.title: UniCache: Unifying Prefix Cache Eviction for Heterogeneous LLM Serving Workloads
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Measurement and Analysis of Computing Systems
candidates.abstract: Prefix caching is a key performance optimization in Large Language Model (LLM) serving systems, enabling reuse of attention Key-Value (KV) states across requests with shared prompt prefixes. However, the size of GPU memory limits cache capacity, making the eviction policy a critical factor in overall system performance. Existing systems primarily rely on simple heuristics, such as LRU, and apply the same policy across task categories, implicitly assuming homogeneous workloads. In practice, however, modern LLMs serve heterogeneous workloads that mix multi-turn conversational traffic with diverse single-turn API requests, leading to fundamentally different prefix reuse patterns. In this work, we first design a trace-driven prefix cache simulator built on vLLM to systematically characterize prefix reuse across representative workloads. Our analysis reveals two dominant reuse patterns---session reuse and structural reuse---that vary significantly across task types. Motivated by these observations, we propose UniCache, a unified eviction policy that jointly captures both reuse patterns and dynamically balances cache allocation across tasks. When implemented in vLLM, UniCache achieves substantial improvements under heterogeneous workloads, improving prefix cache hit rates by up to 17.32% and reducing inference latency by up to 3.63× compared to existing policies.
candidates.reason: 異種LLMサービングワークロードのセッション再利用と構造再利用を捉えプレフィックスキャッシュ追い出しを統一するUniCacheは、サービング中核のキャッシュ政策である。

candidates.title: An Adaptive Prediction of Tokens Fluctuation for Decoupled Prefetching to Accelerate Long-Context LLM Decoding
candidates.abstract: The prohibitively slow speed of long-context LLM decoding is a critical bottleneck, caused by massive Key-Value (KV) access that saturates memory bandwidth. Existing solutions fail due to a fundamental trade-off: static predictors cannot handle the Tokens Fluctuation, leading to permanent accuracy loss from irreversible eviction, while an on-the-fly scoring method creates a synchronous bottleneck that stalls the entire pipeline. This paper presents a co-designed system that breaks this trade-off by leveraging an Adaptive Prediction algorithm to enable a fully Decoupled Prefetching architecture. The proposed Adaptive Prediction model first mirrors the nature of Tokens Fluctuation, enabling a lightweight, reuse-based recovery mechanism that solves irreversible eviction. This high-fidelity prediction then unlocks the Decoupled Prefetching system, which completely hides data transfer latency and eliminates the synchronous bottleneck. On long-context LLM decoding tasks, the proposed system matches the accuracy of a full KV cache with just 256 tokens, while achieving an average 2.50x end-to-end speedup.
candidates.reason: 長文脈LLMデコードでトークン変動に適応する分離型プリフェッチによりKVアクセスの帯域律速を緩和する提案であり、LLMデコード高速化へ直接貢献する。

candidates.title: GPU Acceleration of TFHE-Based High-Precision Nonlinear Layers for Encrypted LLM Inference
candidates.abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) as cloud services raises privacy concerns as inference may leak sensitive data. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) allows computation on encrypted data, but current FHE methods struggle with efficient and precise nonlinear function evaluation. Specifically, CKKS-based approaches require high-degree polynomial approximations, which are costly when target precision increases. Alternatively, TFHE's Programmable Bootstrapping (PBS) outperforms CKKS by offering exact lookup-table evaluation. But it lacks high-precision implementations of LLM nonlinear layers and underutilizes GPU resources. We propose \emph{TIGER}, the first GPU-accelerated framework for high-precision TFHE-based nonlinear LLM layer evaluation. TIGER offers: (1) GPU-optimized WoP-PBS method combined with numerical algorithms to surpass native lookup-table precision limits on nonlinear functions; (2) high-precision and efficient implementations of key nonlinear layers, enabling practical encrypted inference; (3) batch-driven design exploiting inter-input parallelism to boost GPU efficiency. TIGER achieves 7.17$\times$, 16.68$\times$, and 17.05$\times$ speedups over a CPU baseline for GELU, Softmax, and LayerNorm, respectively.
candidates.reason: TFHE暗号化LLM推論の高精度非線形層をGPUで加速する研究であり、秘匿化したままのLLM推論実行という推論システムのボトルネックへ直接取り組んでいる。

candidates.title: Surfing the Activation Wave: Analyzing the Information and Geometry of LLM Hidden States for Speculative Decoding
candidates.abstract: Decoder hidden states from different layers of large language models (LLMs) often encode complementary information. However, existing speculative decoding methods typically rely on a small set of target-model layers chosen using fixed, position-based heuristics. Selecting an optimal subset of layers is inherently a combinatorial problem, making exhaustive evaluation infeasible even for moderately deep models. In this work, we present a principled framework for multi-layer hidden-state selection for speculative decoding based on two complementary criteria: informativeness, measured through matrix-entropy analysis, and diversity, quantified using centered kernel alignment (CKA). We investigate layer-wise Shannon entropy, aggregate entropy under hidden-state concatenation, and pairwise CKA dynamics across depth, revealing distinct geometric and informational compartments within decoder representations. Motivated by these findings, we propose entropy and CKA-based layer selection algorithms that favor hidden-state sets that are both highly informative and minimally redundant. As part of this framework, we introduce token-entropy filtering, which removes hidden states associated with low predictive-entropy tokens, thereby improving the quality of layer-selection statistics. In EAGLE3-style speculative decoding, our selected sets outperform fixed baseline choices, including the default $[2, N//2, N-3]$ rule, while providing a clearer explanation of why some defaults can remain competitive. Our results provide a practical recipe for multi-layer hidden-state selection for speculative decoding, insights into the geometry and information in LLM decoder states, and a foundation for extending similar analysis to related applications.
candidates.reason: LLMの複数層隠れ状態の情報量と多様性をエントロピーとCKAで測り投機的デコード用ドラフタの層選択を設計する研究で、投機的デコード高速化へ直接寄与する。

candidates.title: Give the Drafter a Second Chance to Guess: Parallel Reconsideration for Speculative Decoding
candidates.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference with a small drafter, whose per-guess acceptance rate determines the achievable speedup. Feature-level drafters share a design choice: every token, easy or hard, is drafted under a single forward pass. Many of the tokens the target rejects are ones the drafter is itself unsure about yet the target answers decisively. To address this, we introduce Parallel Reconsideration: guided by its own uncertainty, the drafter reconsiders its hesitant guesses with extra passes that run in parallel with the one-pass draft, adding negligible latency. A co-designed training recipe and serving-time drafting algorithm append these reconsidered guesses to the original draft tree as refined candidates. Across models and benchmarks, on average, Parallel Reconsideration improves over the baselines by 5.3% to 10.2% on acceptance length and by 3.5% to 9.2% on speedup.
candidates.reason: 投機的デコードでドラフタ自身が不確かなトークンへ並列な再検討機会を与える方式は、受理率を上げLLM推論を直接高速化するデコード機構である。
